8251fab7a9f4c561d24b5f088f3002d0070177e6.summary: Doctor Web, a Russian anti-virus company, reported on 22 August 2012 a backdoor it named Mac.BackDoor.Wirenet.1. It described it as the first cross-platform backdoor to run on both Linux and Mac OS X. The backdoor logs keystrokes and steals passwords stored by several browsers, mail clients and chat applications. It uses AES to communicate with its control server. The report did not yet say how it spreads. Doctor Web's products detect and remove it.

82c459aa6c5ad1880851e4fcaed3a989434caf3a.summary: Malpedia family page for RokRAT, a backdoor the page says is commonly distributed as an encoded binary that is downloaded and decrypted by shellcode after weaponized documents are exploited. Listed capabilities include screenshots, keystroke logging, anti-virtual machine checks and cloud storage APIs. The page lists third-party reports from 2017 to 2025 that link RokRAT to APT37, ScarCruft and related names. These attributions come from report titles, not from the page itself.
